claims.paper: rewrite (brief Phase 5): what TRACE documentation contains
claims.claim: TRACE documents record a model's problem formulation, description, data evaluation, conceptual evaluation, implementation verification, output verification, analysis and output corroboration
claims.note: Full text not obtained. The abstract (IDEAS) says TRACE is re-defined as a tool for planning, performing and documenting good modelling practice; that TRACE documents should give convincing evidence that a model was thoughtfully designed, correctly implemented, thoroughly tested, well understood and appropriately used for its intended purpose; and that the updated format follows the 'evaludation' framework. The abstract does not list the elements. The eight-element structure is confirmed only in the stand-in (NEW_Grimm_etal_2020, Supplement S6, which states it uses this paper's structure).

notes: Recommendation for the rewrite: cite TRACE through what was read in full. Grimm et al. 2020 (JASSS, open access) describes TRACE as 'a standard format for documenting all elements of model development, including parameterization, model analysis, and model evaludation' (para. 2.4) and as a format for supplements (para. 5.8); its Supplement S6 compiles two TRACE documents built on this paper's structure, whose eight elements are 1 Problem formulation, 2 Model description, 3 Data evaluation, 4 Conceptual model evaluation, 5 Implementation verification, 6 Model output verification, 7 Model analysis, 8 Model output corroboration (S6 p. 3, definitions on pp. 4-47); Supplement S7 gives a main-text checklist taken from TRACE. Cite Grimm et al. 2014 only as the source of the format, without page-level claims, unless the full text is fetched by hand (the DOI above).
